ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Kamphaeng Phet 2026 — Eat Like the Locals
ogDesc: Ancient-style pad thai with crispy pork instead of peanuts, sea-jellyfish yen ta fo, fresh boneless Ping River fish, 70-year-old fresh noodles, Salobat souvenirs, and a riverside café with sunset views — 10 local favorites in Kamphaeng Phet with prices and planning tips.
eyebrow: Eat like the locals in Kamphaeng Phet · Updated 2026
intro: Kamphaeng Phet is a city where you can eat well without competing with anyone. Pad thai on the Nakhon Chum side uses crispy pork skin instead of peanuts; yen ta fo comes with large chunks of sea jellyfish; Ping River fish arrives fresh and boneless; and there's a riverside café where you can sit watching the sunset for an entire afternoon. We've gathered 10 spots where locals actually eat — in case you're visiting the Historical Park and need a good meal nearby.
chips: 🍜 Ancient-style pad thai with crispy pork
🦐 Yen ta fo with sea jellyfish chunks

blocks.html:
If you had to describe the charm of eating in Kamphaeng Phet in a few words, start with the "Nakhon Chum side" — the vintage market along the Ping River that's the origin of ancient-style pad thai made with crispy pork skin instead of peanuts, and local food you genuinely can't find anywhere else. Cross the bridge to the old-town district and you're in the territory of long-established legendary restaurants: fresh handmade noodles, bold yen ta fo, and a Ping River fish restaurant that proudly offers fresh, mud-free fish. In the evenings the city shifts mode — riverside cafés and a craft beer bar let you sit back and catch the river breeze. It's a city where you can eat from morning to night within a radius of just a few kilometers.

This list has several legendary spots. Charoen Pochana at Salobat Market has been open for over 65 years — famous for its oyster fritters with crab filling and its house-recipe pounded pork, so beloved it appeared on the Krua Khun Toi TV show and became a souvenir people pull over on the highway to buy. Kinpla Thung Setthi holds a LINE MAN Wongnai Users' Choice 2021 award, using primarily Ping River fish. Siang Bamee on Ratchadamnoen 1 Road has made handmade noodles passed down through generations for over 70 years. And Jae Kiao yen ta fo, with its large sea-jellyfish chunks, has become one of the city's signature dishes. Finish reading, then pick which restaurant to start with.

blocks.name: Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum
blocks.signature: Ancient-style pad thai with crispy pork skin, rad na, pad see ew, pork satay
blocks.descHtml:
If you ask Kamphaeng Phet locals which pad thai place comes to mind first, Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum always comes up. A tiny one-room shophouse in an old wooden row building in the middle of Nakhon Chum vintage market, selling ancient-style pad thai passed down through the family from grandma's generation for over fifty years — back when there was no bridge over the Ping River and people from the city side still crossed over just to eat here. Perfect for anyone who wants to try genuinely local food from Nakhon Chum, or for visitors who've crossed the bridge to explore the old town and want a proper dinner.

What makes this stall unlike anywhere else is the use of crispy pork skin instead of ground peanuts. Mixed with hot noodles, the crispy pork softens and melts in the mouth, beautifully rich and fragrant. Served with fresh vegetables — garlic chives, bean sprouts, and mustard greens — all unlimited. The essential order is the ancient-style pad thai; those coming in groups can add rad na and pad see ew to share. Glass noodle pad thai is also available, and out front there's a pork satay cart with fishballs and sweets to snack on while you wait.

Most reviews agree: the noodles are perfectly chewy, not soggy — seasoned just right so you barely need to add anything, with the fragrance of an old-style wok. Many say this kind of flavor is genuinely hard to find anywhere else now. Prices are very friendly — about 30–35 THB a plate, and one person can eat well under 100 THB. The atmosphere is a simple old-school stall — nothing fancy, but with a warm nostalgic feeling.

Worth knowing: the stall opens in the evening, roughly 5:45 to 9pm. There's a queue at peak time because it gets busy, but regulars say it's worth the wait — each plate of noodles is freshly stir-fried to order, so patience is needed. Coming by car, park near the market and walk in from under the bridge, turn right, the stall is on your left. Come hungry — you'll want to order more than one dish.
mustOrder: Ancient-style pad thai with crispy pork skin
blocks.bestFor: Evening local food after exploring the old town
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: pad thai · Takeaway / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Jae Kiao Yen Ta Fo (Sea Jellyfish) Kamphaeng Phet
blocks.signature: Yen ta fo with large sea-jellyfish chunks, seafood noodle soup, fresh coconut water
blocks.descHtml:
If yen ta fo in Kamphaeng Phet comes up in conversation, Jae Kiao Yen Ta Fo (Sea Jellyfish) is the place locals nominate as their go-to. Tucked in a small soi off Rajawithi Road (Wijit 2, Soi 1) in the city center, the standout feature is a rich, deep pink yen ta fo broth — tangy-forward with a well-rounded finish. Many reviewers say the same thing: "delicious without needing any extra seasoning" — just lift the bowl and drink. Perfect for anyone who wants a boldly flavored noodle soup in an authentic local setting.

The essential order is the yen ta fo with large sea-jellyfish chunks — the house signature. Fresh jellyfish, crunchy, in generous pieces, not fishy at all. Topped with fish dumplings, shrimp balls, crispy wontons — and a seafood combo version for those who want to try more. For a snack, there's blanched jellyfish with seafood dipping sauce. Close with fresh coconut water — natural sweetness, refreshing, and it cuts through the richness perfectly. Noodle choice covers thin, vermicelli, and wide; available in both broth and dry versions.

Prices are very friendly — noodles start around 50 THB a bowl, coconut water 20 THB. Eating well here costs nothing. The shop is clean, with parking nearby. Open approximately 09:30–15:00, closed Monday and Tuesday. Plan for mid-morning through afternoon — dishes can sell out on busy days. Wongnai rates it at 4.3 stars. Most reviewers come with friends or family for a light, satisfying lunch.
mustOrder: Yen ta fo with large sea-jellyfish chunks
blocks.bestFor: Tangy-forward lunch with friends or family

blocks.name: Siang Bamee
blocks.area: Ratchadamnoen 1 Road, Nai Mueang Subdistrict, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet District
blocks.signature: House-made fresh egg noodles with wontons, dry tom yam bamee, thin-skinned wonton soup
blocks.descHtml:
Siang Bamee is a chrysanthemum-noodle shop that has been part of Kamphaeng Phet for many decades. The name "Siang" comes from the original grandfather who created the recipe, and his descendants have continued passing it down through generations. For anyone driving through Kamphaeng Phet who wants a bowl of old-style noodles — handmade, cooked to order — this is the first name locals mention. A natural choice for breakfast or lunch before heading north.

The most talked-about dishes are the house-made fresh egg noodle wontons, dry tom yam bamee, and thin-skinned wonton soup. The real star is the noodles themselves — reviewers consistently say they're cooked just right, springy, with satisfying chew. The dry bamee arrives pre-seasoned with red pork, minced pork, liver, and fried garlic — traditional style. Wontons are wrapped in thin pastry with a generous filling. The broth is slightly sweet and mild — suitable for children and adults alike. Season further with fish sauce, sugar, and fresh lime left at the table.

Prices are very accessible — mostly under 100 THB per person, dry bamee starting around 35 THB, wonton soup around 55 THB. Pork satay can be added for a side order. The shop is an old shophouse, simple and unpretentious — more seating than it looks from outside. Open daily 08:00–15:00. Located on Ratchadamnoen 1 Road in the old town — easy to find, but roadside parking is limited. On weekend mornings expect to circle a bit for a spot.

This shop stays popular because it's a legendary noodle house for the province — handmade noodles, unchanged recipe. Kamphaeng Phet people feel attached to it and keep bringing visitors to try it. Worth knowing: the flavor leans classic and simple. Those who prefer bold flavors may find some dishes mild — try the noodles plain first, then season to taste, to fully appreciate the character of handmade noodles in the old style.
blocks.bestFor: Breakfast or lunch — legendary noodles in the morning

blocks.name: Janpha
blocks.signature: Salted-egg som tam Thai and northern-style laab with stir-fried pork
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to sit long, eat bold food, and listen to live music one evening in Kamphaeng Phet, Janpha is the first name locals tend to mention. It sits on Charoen Suk Road opposite Robinson department store — easy to find, with parking right in front. As evening sets in and the lights come on, tables fill up and the atmosphere becomes a relaxed hybrid of restaurant and chill spot, with a live band playing across genres to accompany the meal. A popular meeting point for groups of friends and families who want a long, unhurried dinner.

The heart of Janpha is its bold Isan and Northern Thai food. The salted-egg som tam Thai is a dish many people come back for repeatedly — the papaya shreds are pounded to a sour-sweet-salty balance, with the salted egg yolk folding in beautifully. The northern-style laab with stir-fried pork is another standout — stir-fried until fragrant, eaten with hot sticky rice, it's hard to stop. Those who love the bold-and-savory profile can anchor the table with laab and tom saeb as the core dishes.

The other dishes hold up just as well. Mackerel fried rice that reviewers repeatedly call more fragrant and flavorful than expected. Crispy chicken wings — crunchy outside, tender inside. Marinated pork neck and grilled beef. Cold fish sauce-pickled shrimp for those who like a sharp, cool flavor. Prices per head remain accessible — ordering multiple dishes to share across the table is still comfortable. Well-suited to group dining.

Janpha is open daily from late morning through the evening. There's an active Facebook page with regular updates, and delivery is available. For anyone visiting Kamphaeng Phet who wants a dinner that combines good food and a relaxed local atmosphere, this is the answer — sit long, order som tam, order laab, and let the music carry the evening.
blocks.bestFor: Dinner with a group of friends or family — chill, live music, bold Isan food
blocks.zone: Charoen Suk Road (opposite Robinson Kamphaeng Phet)
blocks.foodType: Isan/Northern Thai — eat and drink with live music

blocks.name: Kinpla Thung Setthi
blocks.area: Nakhon Chum Subdistrict, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet District
blocks.signature: Boneless Ping River fish, deep-fried pla kod kang with garlic, stir-fried pla thephao with holy basil, tom yam pla kod kang
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving through Kamphaeng Phet and want a proper freshwater fish meal, Kinpla Thung Setthi is the restaurant locals and passing travellers mention most. It sits alongside Phahon Yothin Road at the Thung Setthi intersection in Nakhon Chum subdistrict — a large sign on the main road makes it easy to spot. The selling point is Ping River fish, caught fresh, with firm flesh and none of the muddy smell you get from farmed fish. The restaurant's tagline — "Nothing but fish, no bones to bother you" — is a real selling point for families. Perfect for a group or family who wants a proper sit-down meal, and for anyone who doesn't enjoy picking out bones.

The dishes people order again and again include pla kod kang poached and served with dipping sauce — springy flesh that pairs perfectly with seafood sauce — and pla kod kang tom yam, a broth you can keep drinking. Fish cake made from spotted featherback (tord man pla krai) comes bouncy and fresh, while stir-fried pla thephao with holy basil is a crowd favourite. Those who like bold flavours can try pla kod kang stir-fried with galangal or snakehead fish with three-sauce gravy. Reviews consistently praise the fish as tender, the fried dishes as crunchy outside and tender inside, and several preparations come pre-deboned for convenience. The flavour profile is homestyle Thai — intense and satisfying.

Most dishes are priced 100–280 THB; average spend is roughly 101–250 THB per head. Some feel the premium fish dishes are worth every baht; a few think certain specials run a little high. The atmosphere is a roadside restaurant — open, spacious, with easy parking. Open daily approximately 09:30–20:00 with a break roughly 14:30–16:00. If you're planning a lunch stop, check the hours before arriving.

The restaurant's fame goes beyond word of mouth — it has appeared on the Krua Khun Toi TV show and won the Wongnai Users' Choice award, making it a firm destination for fish lovers in Kamphaeng Phet. Worth knowing: weekends and holidays get busy and tables may have a wait. Coming as a group and ordering multiple dishes to share is the best-value way to eat here.
mustOrder: Pla kod kang poached with dipping sauce
Stir-fried pla thephao with holy basil
blocks.bestFor: Group or family outing for freshwater fish lovers

Choose a stay near the city center or along the Ping River — you can walk the Nakhon Chum market in the evening, drop by a riverside café, and get back to your room in minutes. blocks.name: Tiaw Ruea Aeb Saeb
blocks.signature: Boat noodles with braised pork nam tok, mama noodles with pork nam tok, wide noodle with meatballs, herbal drink
blocks.descHtml:
If you're exploring the old town area of Kamphaeng Phet along Thesha 1 Road and feel like a bowl of homestyle boat noodles, this is the place people quietly pass on to each other. The name "Tiaw Ruea Aeb Saeb" — roughly "sneak-attack boat noodles that punch above their weight" — is a playful pun on the shop's style: it's tucked away in a shophouse on a one-way street, not prominently visible from a main road. The owner sold noodles in Bangkok for years before moving back to open near home, so the Bangkok boat noodle style came along too. Perfect for a light, affordable lunch — easy solo or comfortable for a family ordering to share.

The dishes people order most are the boat noodles with braised pork nam tok — broth slow-cooked to a rich, rounded depth, loaded with pork, liver, Chinese sausage, and the braised pork tender enough to almost dissolve. Another popular order is mama noodles with pork nam tok — instant noodles cooked with house boat noodle broth, bold and satisfying. Those who prefer wide noodles can get wide noodle with meatballs — springy balls, a generously topped bowl. While waiting, get the fried spring rolls or crispy oyster mushrooms — both come crunchy. Then cool down with the house-made herbal drink, gently sweet and refreshing.

The atmosphere is a small, home-style shop — the service feels like a relative feeding you. Most reviews praise the value: every dish under 100 THB and satisfying, which is why it earned a Kamphaeng Phet Good Stuff certificate. Regular customers keep coming back. Google rates it around 4.3 stars.

Worth knowing: the shop opens 09:00–15:00 and is closed on Wednesdays. It's on a one-way street and parking is tight. If you're coming on a weekend lunchtime, arriving early or on a weekday is more comfortable. Some dishes sell out before closing. If you specifically want something, before 2pm is safer. Once you factor in the price and this quality of flavor, it's clear why regulars come back again and again.
mustOrder: Boat noodles with braised pork nam tok
Mama noodles with pork nam tok

blocks.name: Banyakad Cafe' & Restaurant
blocks.area: Nai Mueang Subdistrict, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet District
blocks.signature: Coffee and bakery by the water, beautifully plated main courses, Ping River sunset views
blocks.descHtml:
Banyakad Cafe' & Restaurant is a café and restaurant on the Ping River in central Kamphaeng Phet that many people nominate as their go-to meeting point for a long, leisurely afternoon. The building has a European-glass-house-meets-nature feel, divided into two distinct seating zones: an air-conditioned indoor section, and an outdoor riverside area with canvas daybeds where you can recline and watch the Ping River flow. Whether you're coming as a couple, a family, or a group of friends, there's space. Parking is generous, no need to circle.

The coffee and bakery section is the lead act during the day. Reviewers describe the iced latte as fragrant, strong, and alert-making. Those with a sweet tooth can try coconut cake, red velvet, and strawberry smoothies — visually appealing and not overly sweet. As evening approaches, the restaurant shifts to beautifully plated main courses: ribeye steak, salmon steak, BBQ ribs, stir-fried shrimp pasta — covering Thai, Western, and Italian. The standout menu item that many reviewers mention is the tom yam kung, which reviewers say tastes perfectly rounded alongside the riverside setting.

The real highlight is the sunset — golden light gradually falling onto the Ping River as evening comes in. The riverside photo spots fill with guests raising cameras. Some evenings there's soft live music. Beverages and bakery items are priced like a regular café; main courses step up a little in line with the ingredients. Google rates the restaurant around 4.5 stars from hundreds of reviewers, reflecting broad satisfaction with both the views and the food.

Worth knowing before you go: open 10:30–22:00. On holiday evenings it gets busy. If you're coming as a group or specifically want a riverside table, calling ahead to reserve is worth it. Some reviews note that service during peak crowds can slow down, and a few dishes feel slightly expensive. But overall it remains one of the Ping River cafés that Kamphaeng Phet locals and visitors come back to regularly.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside dinner watching the sunset — couples or families

blocks.name: Kittipochana
blocks.signature: Crispy pork yam, oyster fritters / crab fritters, Hong Kong noodles, tofu with toppings
blocks.descHtml:
When long-established Kamphaeng Phet restaurants come up — the kind locals take older relatives to for a proper sit-down meal — Kittipochana is one of the first names mentioned. A traditional Chinese restaurant open for nearly 50 years, passed down from grandfather to children to grandchildren, now run by the third generation. Located on Wijit 2 Road in the city center, it's well-suited for families, large groups, and banquet meals where a revolving round table is the point — ordering dishes to share around the table together.

The most frequently mentioned dish in reviews is the crispy pork yam with cucumber — large, satisfying pieces of crispy pork tossed in a moist dressing, with fresh cucumber, and generous peanuts. Reviewers say the flavour has stayed the same for decades. The next essential order is the oyster fritters / crab fritters: firm filling, fried until the outside is crunchy while inside stays tender, dipped in sweet plum sauce. The Hong Kong noodles loaded with toppings — soft noodles, full of vegetables, light Chinese-style seasoning — and the tofu with toppings are both recommended house specialties. For those who want something bolder, adding a mixed seafood yam brings instant punch.

The overall flavour profile is authentic Chinese — rounded rather than intense. Those who prefer strong flavours may find some dishes lean mild, but the strong points are generous portions, consistent quality, and the reliability of a long-established Chinese restaurant. Per-head pricing around 101–250 THB; main dishes start in the hundreds. Reasonable for a restaurant of this standing. Air-conditioned, decorated in old-style Chinese restaurant fashion.

Open daily in two sittings: 10:00–14:00 and 16:00–21:00. The restaurant also handles private Chinese banquet catering. Worth knowing: the shop is at a busy corner junction, and parking can be tight during peak hours. If arriving as a large group at lunch or dinner, allowing extra time for parking or calling ahead to book a table is a good idea.
blocks.bestFor: Family or banquet meal — Chinese round-table style

blocks.name: Whats Your Name Cafe & Craft Beer
blocks.signature: Intense matcha, signature coffee, croffles, draft craft beer in the evening
blocks.descHtml:
If you're visiting Kamphaeng Phet and want a café that works all day, Whats Your Name Cafe & Craft Beer is the place a local friend would take you first. The concept runs two modes in one: daytime is a fully equipped coffee-matcha café; come evening it transforms into a relaxed draft craft beer bar. The interior is loft-style — exposed concrete walls, high ceilings in dark tones, offset by a circular glass window opening outdoors and tall plants. Every angle photographs well. Perfect for café-design lovers, photo-lovers, and groups of friends who want to sit until late.

The most talked-about item is the matcha — reviewers consistently say it's dense and full-bodied, with a real umami kick, sweetness adjustable to preference. Those who want deep green intensity love it. The coffee is also well-made, with multiple bean options; baristas can guide you toward chocolate-nut or fruity profiles. The snack to pair with coffee is the croffle. Then as evening sets in, shift to draft craft beer — cocktails and wine are also available — and the atmosphere transitions from café to bar, seamlessly.

Prices are friendly — most drinks in the 60–120 THB range, reasonable for this quality of space and atmosphere. A few reviews note that some menu items feel a little pricey, but overall it's comfortable. Location: 250/53 Moo 6, Sa Kaeo Subdistrict, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet — central, easy to find, parking in front. Open daily from 07:30 to around 22:00. Early openers appreciate this: it opens earlier than most cafés in the city.

The reason Whats Your Name stays popular is that it does everything in one place — good morning coffee, intense matcha through the day, and draft beer to settle into for the evening. Worth knowing: from evening onward the atmosphere shifts to a bar — if you're coming with family or children, the daytime slot is more comfortable. On some Tuesdays the shop may adjust hours or close — check their page before heading out to be sure.
blocks.bestFor: Café-lover and photographer — sit all day into an evening of craft beer

blocks.name: Jae Kiao Branch / Khrua Rim Khlong (Khlong Suan Mak Canal) Nakhon Chum
blocks.area: Rim Khlong Suan Mak Canal, Nakhon Chum Subdistrict, Mueang Kamphaeng Phet District
blocks.signature: Deep-fried pla rak kluay, freshwater fish dishes, local home-style food, canal-side atmosphere
blocks.descHtml:
Khrua Rim Khlong (Khlong Suan Mak Canal) Nakhon Chum is a traditional home-style restaurant on the water that Kamphaeng Phet people think of when they want fresh river fish in a shaded, relaxed setting. The restaurant is tucked into a small soi along Suan Mak Canal on the Nakhon Chum side. Tables are arranged in individual shaded pavilions under trees, with views of flowing water. Ideal for families coming in groups, groups of friends, or anyone who wants to escape the noise and eat at a long, comfortable pace.

The hero dishes are the freshwater fish menu — steamed, stir-fried, curried, and fried across a wide range. Deep-fried pla rak kluay — crispy outside, tender inside — is a house specialty many order as a snack while waiting for mains. Tom yam pla kod kang with a thick broth, and stir-fried hot-chili pla thephao are two dishes reviewers mention most, consistently calling the fish fresh, the flavors bold and intense. There's also a house-recipe steamed egg with bao, fresh-fish cake, three-layered pork fried with fish sauce, spicy shrimp salad, and frog with garlic and pepper for those who want variety.

Prices are friendly — most dishes 140–200 THB, average roughly 101–250 THB per head. Orders including larger fish or big-table dining will run a little higher. Open daily 09:00–22:00, with parking on both sides of the restaurant. The entrance is near the U-turn bend at the base of Nakhon Chum Bridge — easy to spot.

What keeps people coming back is the combination of home-style cooking and natural canal-side atmosphere in one place. One small note: evenings by the water bring mosquitoes, as expected at any canal-side restaurant — bring repellent and the evening becomes much more comfortable. If you're coming as a weekend group or want a specific waterside table, calling ahead to book is worth it for the better spots.
blocks.bestFor: Family riverside meal — freshwater fish lovers

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Kamphaeng Phet

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Kamphaeng Phet doesn't have Grab coverage like a big city. Restaurants are spread across both the old-town side and the Nakhon Chum side — two different banks of the Ping River. Renting a car or motorbike is the most flexible option. Within the Nakhon Chum market area, walking and exploring on foot is easy.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Street stalls and old-school noodle restaurants mostly take cash or PromptPay. Bring small bills and coins — many shops have no card machine. Cafés and larger restaurants usually accept QR payment.

items.title: Beat the rush
items.text: Noodle shops and souvenir spots open in the morning and tend to sell out early — before noon is safest. Pad thai and riverside cafés fill up on holiday evenings. Allow extra time, or arrive early.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Most local restaurants here have Thai-only menus. Open Google Translate with the camera to read ahead, or point at food photos at the shop front. Kamphaeng Phet people are friendly — smile and ask, it works.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Street stalls and noodle shops don't expect tips — pay the menu price and you're done. At cafés or sit-down restaurants with table service, leaving a little change is a kind gesture but not expected.

items.title: Try the local specialties
items.text: While you're in Kamphaeng Phet, don't miss the ancient-style pad thai with crispy pork skin — it's genuinely a local flavour you won't find elsewhere — and fresh Ping River fish. These are regional tastes that are hard to replicate anywhere else.

blocks.title: Planning a full day of eating in Kamphaeng Phet
blocks.html:
Start early at Siang Bamee on Ratchadamnoen 1 Road — this shop opens from morning through afternoon and tends to sell out fast. Getting there before noon is the safer bet. Follow with Jae Kiao yen ta fo in the city for a bold midday bowl, then cross to the Nakhon Chum side in the late afternoon to wait for Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum, which opens in the evening.

If you're driving through Khanuburi Woralak District, stop in at Charoen Pochana at Salobat Market to pick up oyster fritters with crab and pounded pork as a souvenir for the road — the shop opens through afternoon and trades Monday to Saturday. Close the day at Banyakad Cafe on the Ping River to catch the sunset, or go to Whats Your Name for evening craft beer if you prefer a night-out atmosphere.

blocks.text: Planning multiple restaurant stops in Kamphaeng Phet? Book a stay near the old town first — it makes the evening pad thai stall and a riverside sunset café both easy to reach, without rushing.

faq.q: Which restaurant is most famous in Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: By reputation and word of mouth, Charoen Pochana at Salobat Market is a 65-year-old institution famous for its oyster fritters with crab filling and pounded pork — it appeared on a national TV cooking show and became a signature souvenir. Kinpla Thung Setthi won the LINE MAN Wongnai Users' Choice award in 2021. And Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum is the ancient-style pad thai that visitors keep coming to try.

faq.q: What are the local specialties of Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: The must-try local specialty is the ancient-style pad thai from Nakhon Chum, made with crispy pork skin instead of peanuts — find it at Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum in Nakhon Chum market. Fresh Ping River fish served boneless is another highlight, available at restaurants like Kinpla Thung Setthi. Jae Kiao's yen ta fo with large sea-jellyfish chunks is a city signature. And for souvenirs, pounded pork and crab oyster fritters from Salobat are what passing drivers always stop for.

faq.q: How expensive is eating in Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: Very accessible. Noodle shops and local street food like Supap pad thai start around 30–35 THB per dish; yen ta fo and boat noodles are around 50–90 THB. Fish restaurants charge about 100–280 THB per dish. Riverside cafés have drinks from around 60–120 THB, with main courses stepping up by menu.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: Most noodle shops and street stalls are walk-in on weekdays — just sit down. On holiday evenings, popular spots like Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum and Jae Kiao yen ta fo can have long queues — allow time. For riverside cafés like Banyakad at sunset, calling ahead for a waterside table is worth it.

faq.q: Which places are open in the evening or at night?
faq.a: Supap Pad Thai Nakhon Chum opens in the evening at the Nakhon Chum market. Banyakad Cafe stays open until around 10pm for a long riverside sit. Whats Your Name becomes a craft beer bar from evening and stays open late. In contrast, noodle shops and souvenir shops like Siang Bamee and Charoen Pochana focus on morning through afternoon hours — check each card before heading out.
